claims.explanation: WZ-4002 is a dual EGFR/ERBB2 kinase inhibitor, and the selectively killed lines are enriched for EGFR-mutant lung cancer (HCC4006, PC14) and other EGFR/ERBB2-pathway-activated or EGFR-overexpressing epithelial tumors, while the least affected lines are enriched for KRAS/BRAF/NF1-driven MAPK-pathway tumors that bypass EGFR dependence. Selectivity therefore most plausibly reflects oncogene addiction to EGFR/ERBB2 signaling, with EGFR mutation/amplification and high EGFR or ERBB2 expression sensitizing and downstream RAS/MAPK activation (KRAS, BRAF, NF1) conferring protection.

features.basis: EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC4006, PC14) are among the most killed; EGFR kinase mutations sensitize to EGFR inhibitors
EGFR/ERBB2 are the annotated drug targets; high receptor expression increases dependence on EGFR signaling
ERBB2 is a direct WZ-4002 target; ERBB2-driven/overexpressing tumors depend on ERBB2 kinase activity
clinically observed ERBB2 kinase-domain mutations show differential sensitivity to ERBB2 inhibitors
KRAS-mutant lines (RERFLCAD1, SW1573, OV7, TCCPAN2) are among the least affected, consistent with MAPK-pathway bypass of EGFR dependence
BRAF-mutant lines (LOXIMVI, G361, WM793, HT115, CAL12T) are enriched among least affected, indicating downstream MAPK activation bypasses EGFR/ERBB2 blockade
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK signaling and is frequent in the least-affected lines (KALS1, YD8, COLO792, RD, FTC133, LCLC103H, HT115)
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT signaling downstream of RTKs and appears in several least-affected lines (KALS1, FTC133, WM793)
PIK3CA mutation can drive PI3K-pathway dependence independent of EGFR/ERBB2, seen in least-affected lines (SW1573, BT474, HT115)
TP53 mutation is nearly ubiquitous across both groups and thus not selective; listed only to note lack of discriminating value
